correctness.rationale: Two proved universal mask lemmas imply exact equality of nonnegative separation constraints. Opposite-shore pairs are automatically distinguished by every vertex. The fractional and all positive integer k statements follow by containment and monotonicity; no converse is assumed without proof. The explicit 7-vertex diameter-four graph has seven distinct edge distance vectors but a repeated vertex vector. Standalone finite verifier exhaustively validates the mask lemmas on 8701 connected small bipartite instances and the boundary witness; finite checks support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Five distinct semantic queries against the mathematical research index and targeted external searches were compared with full mathematical statements in the founding 2016 paper, projective incidence literature and three closest published mathematical findings. Their specialized scalar/count results do not imply the universal equality of all vertex and edge separation constraints, nor fractional/k-hierarchy identity. Possible differently named prior theorem remains a residual risk, and inaccessible full papers were not claimed inspected.
residual_risks: The simple general separation-mask theorem may already appear under alternative terminology in unindexed historical literature; search absence is not a novelty proof.
The 2020 AIMS paper's complete theorem text was not accessible through its abstract-only representation and thus was not declared not covering.
No independent publication-priority examination or external audit has occurred.

value.rationale: The identity is stronger than coincident scalar dimensions: it equates every feasible resolving set, the full cardinality enumerators, arbitrary fault-tolerant k-levels and fractional feasibility/optimality. It transfers prior work between edge and vertex localization across broad naturally occurring graph families, including all symmetric-design incidence graphs, and gives a sharp universal diameter boundary with an explicit small counterexample.
